question: What should I do if I can't fulfill an oath I made in Allah's name?
asked: I made a promise with someone and mentioned the name of Allah, making an oath in Allah's name. At the time I was sincere and felt I could fulfill it. However, the situation between the two of us deteriorated, and neither he nor I is keeping that promise. I feel very guilty. What can be done?
answer:
Now, he did not tell me what the promise is, and the point is not what it is, but the fact that he made an oath with Allah's name, and now he is unable to fulfill that oath.

So we need to understand: in our religion, invoking Allah's name when you make a promise is a very, very big deal. And our scholars mention that there are three categories of mentioning Allah's name when you make a promise.

The first of them is what is called laghw. Laghw is when you mention the name of Allah and from the context people understand it's not a serious oath; it is simply that you say Allah's name. This is something that is very common in some cultures. For example, you say, "Are you free right now?" "Wallahi, I'm busy right now." This "wallahi, I'm busy" is just an expression. It's not like you are giving a halaf that is serious in nature. "Can you make it on Thursday to have a meeting?" "Wallahi, can we do it another day?" You just say Allah's name because that is the cultural habit.

And in my own experience, I would say, and Allah knows best, that in some cultures it's more common than others, and perhaps in certain cultures it's not that common. So when I say this, people of certain lands say, "It's not something we're accustomed to; we don't do it in our culture." So it's a very cultural thing. In some cultures Allah's name is mentioned every second sentence, you know: wallahi this, wallahi that, wallahi this. Every third thing is wallahi, wallahi; it keeps on like this. So in their culture it is common.

And the verdict is: it is makruh but not haram. You should not mention Allah's name for no reason, but it is not sinful; you're not going to go to Jahannam for this. Everybody understands that when you say "wallahi, I'm busy," it's not like the wallahi you give in a court of law, when people are looking and you say, "I swear by Allah I'm telling the truth." The context is understood.

And Allah mentions in the Qur'an, Surah al-Ma'idah verse 89: Allah is not going to call you to task for your laghw in your ayman. It's not a haram thing. Laghw means you just say it in vain. Yamin is the halaf: in Arabic, yamin means you give an oath, a qasam. In Urdu we say qasam khana, you give the qasam; in Arabic it is called yamin. And the yamin is essentially like the right hand, because it's generally done with the right hand. You raise your right hand in the Western court; on the Eastern side you might shake the person's hand and say, "I swear by the name of Allah." That's why it's called yamin, the seriousness of it; it's called the right hand.

So Allah is saying He will not call you to task for the laghw. If it is laghw, you are not sinful, but it is not encouraged, because you shouldn't just mention the name of Allah for no reason. This is the first category.

The second category is the exact opposite: you say the name of Allah and you mean it, but you are, a'udhu billah, lying. This is called in the hadith al-yamin al-ghamus. Ghamus means the one that inserts you into it, because you go to Jahannam for this yamin. Al-yamin al-ghamus: the oath that will cause you to enter, a'udhu billah, a'udhu billah, Jahannam.

The Prophet ﷺ said, "Should I not tell you of the major sins?" They said, "Yes, ya Rasulallah." So he said, "To do shirk with Allah," and to do this. He was lying on his back, and he got up (not stood up; he was against the wall, and he got up) and he said, "And the false yamin, the yamin al-ghamus, the yamin al-ghamus, the yamin al-ghamus." The false yamin. To show how important it was, he got up and he made this point: to mention the name of Allah knowingly in batil.

And in another version, or another hadith, we learn that, a'udhu billah, there is the la'nah of Allah on the one who uses the name of Allah in a lie. A'udhu billah. There's Allah's la'nah on this person.

Therefore, by unanimous consensus, to say the name of Allah in a lying oath is amongst the major, major sins. And there is no kaffarah other than genuine repentance to Allah. You cannot just make it up by doing something; this is that type of sin. The only thing to make it up is your ikhlas and your tawbah between you and Allah. Otherwise, it is amongst the major sins to mention the name of Allah and to intentionally lie.

And that's why du'a is made against that person in some hadith. For example, of the du'as that are made against this person is the businessman, the merchant, who makes a halaf, an oath with Allah, that he purchased a product for a certain amount, and he's lying, to sell it at a higher profit. So Allah's name is so cheap that he's willing to sell it for a few dollars. How can there be barakah in this person? That person, la'nah has been given, and there is no barakah. So the opposite is al-yamin al-ghamus, and that is to lie intentionally, knowing you are lying, and bringing the name of Allah into it.

And the third category, which is what our brother is asking about, is called al-yamin al-mun'aqidah: the yamin that is a serious yamin, the yamin that is meant to be the real oath in the name of Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala. And Allah mentions in the Qur'an: protect your oaths, when you mention them in the name of Allah. Protect your oaths.

And Allah says in the Qur'an that those who mention the name of Allah in a false yamin, those people, Allah says (listen to this): number one, they have no share of the Akhirah; they'll get nothing. Number two, Allah will not even speak to them; in anger, Allah will not even speak to them. Number three, Allah will not even look at them. Number four, Allah will not purify them. Number five, they shall have a painful torment. What more do you need? What more do you need to warn you? Do not mention the name of Allah in a lie. Never, ever, ever mention the name of Allah knowing that you are lying. This is amongst the greatest, akbar al-kaba'ir, amongst the greatest of all evil deeds.

And in another hadith, the Prophet ﷺ said, akbar al-kaba'ir, the biggest of all evil: number one, he said, committing shirk with Allah. Number two, he said, rejecting your parents, being disrespectful to your parents. Number three, he said, murder. Number four, he said, al-yamin al-ghamus. Just look at the list. After shirk and murder and rejecting parents, what was number four? This yamin. It is next to murder on this list. So be careful, Muslims, when you mention the name of Allah. Be careful.

It is mentioned in our books, in the Kitab al-Zuhd of Imam Ahmad, that 'Isa ibn Maryam was walking on the path and he saw someone steal; he saw someone take another person's property. He said, "O so-and-so, fear Allah, don't steal." The man said, "Wallahi, I didn't steal." 'Isa said, "My eyes are lying, and you spoke the truth." Because you mentioned the name of Allah, I would rather accuse my eyes of lying than accuse you of mentioning Allah's name in vain.

So he retracted, so as not to punish the person; but that's up to Allah. He retracted: I must have lied, my eyes are lying, my eyes didn't see what they saw, and Allah's name is valid. Out of respect for the name of Allah, when he heard the man say, "Wallahi, I didn't steal," he said, "My eyes are lying, and okay, you didn't steal." This shows us the impact of using the name of Allah.

So this is al-yamin al-laghw, al-yamin al-ghamus, and you have al-yamin al-mun'aqidah, which is the effective yamin. What is the effective yamin? The effective yamin is where the context clarifies you mean it. You mean it. And the most obvious example is in a court of law, when the judge says, in this court or in the Islamic court, "Do you swear by Allah you are telling the truth?" This now is a very serious matter. Or there is an argument going on and somebody says, "Ah, you are lying," and now your face changes and you say, "I swear by Allah I am telling the truth." Now you are invoking the name of Allah to bring something serious, so serious that the other person will say, "Okay, he is not going to disrespect that name." Do you understand why it's so important?

So before we even answer the question, I wanted to clarify: this is a big deal, to mention Allah's name. And that is why we need to be careful when we mention Allah's name, and not mention it in vain. It is better to face all the consequences without mentioning Allah's name lying than to mention Allah's name lying and then face the consequences of this dunya and the akhirah.

So the context tells us it is al-yamin al-mun'aqidah, the real yamin. Okay, now the brother says, "I made it sincerely," so this is not al-yamin al-ghamus. He was sincere, and he said whatever it was. Let's give an example: "I promise to visit your house every few weeks," whatever it was; we don't know what it was. He made a promise to Allah. Maybe there was some tension between the two of them (this is what it looks like), then they tried to reconcile, so they mentioned Allah's name and said, "Okay, let us promise by Allah that we will do this and that." And both of them made an actual promise; maybe both of them were sincere. Then, subhanAllah, things happened and the promise is not met.

Here we have two scenarios, with a slight difference in the verdict of either one. So I'm going to take a step back.

The first scenario: you mention the name of Allah in a solemn oath, for something to do with the future, and you are sincere. But time changes, and you think or you feel or you presume that this oath... "I made it and it was a mistake, and something else is better than my oath, overall, in the eyes of Islam and the laws of the Shari'ah. I said it, I meant it at the time, but I regret it and I shouldn't have done it, and I realized that the alternative is better for deen and dunya than what I said." And our Prophet ﷺ said, and the hadith is in Bukhari and Muslim: **if you swear a qasam by Allah, then you see the other alternative better than your qasam, then do the alternative that is better and make kaffarah for your yamin.**

Let me give you a simple example. Sometimes, in a state of anger, you have an argument with somebody and you say, "Wallahi, I will never visit that person's house again," and you mean it. You say it and you mean it. It's not wajib to go to the other person's house, so you made a halaf with Allah. You say, "Wallahi, that person dishonored me, he disrespected me, he said this about me," and you make a qasam. Your family is there, your friends are there, your brother is there: "Wallahi, I will never visit that person's house again."

Now, the yamin is halal, but is it mustahabb, dear Muslims? Is it good? No. What did our Prophet ﷺ say? If you made a yamin, then you realize the other option is better than your yamin. What is the other option in this case? Sulh, correct? The other option is sulh: you forgive and you make up, correct? Our Prophet ﷺ said: don't even hesitate, don't even hesitate; you're choosing the better option. This is, wallahi, a mercy from Allah, because if Allah had wanted to, He could have said, "Khalas, you have to bear the consequences."

And dear Muslims, how often we use the name of Allah in a state of anger, and we mean it, and when we calm down, we regret. How often a husband says to a wife, or a wife says to a husband, "If you do this again, wallahi I will divorce you." A'udhu billah, a'udhu billah, a'udhu billah. That's not a successful marriage. Number one, what type of marriage will be successful when the wife is always threatened with divorce? Number two, you mention Allah's name. Don't do this. You don't mention Allah's name.

In another verse in the Qur'an, Allah says: don't bring in the name of Allah to use in your qasam to do things that are not good. Allah is saying: don't use it, don't use My name in a qasam for something that is not positive. Don't do this, that you're not going to do birr, you're not going to have sulh. Don't bring in My name. "I'm never going to talk to him again": Allah says in the Qur'an, don't bring in My name. But people do. It's not haram, but it is makruh, definitely makruh. You're using Allah's qasam for something that's not positive.

It's not haram because it's not wajib to visit. You understand what I'm saying, right? You understand this point. He's not making a qasam for a haram, "I'm going to drink alcohol," a'udhu billah. He's saying, "I'm not going to visit this person." Visiting that person is not wajib, so he's not sinful. It is a legitimate yamin, a legitimate oath. But now he realizes, "I shouldn't have done that." He calms down, he wants to forgive, but he has mentioned the name of Allah.

This is scenario one: he sees something better. In this case there is no repentance, but there is a kaffarah. Why is there no repentance? Because he's doing the better of the two. His option of qasam was the worse of the two: "I'm not going to visit," "I'm not going to talk," whatever it is, you understand. "I'm going to divorce you": maybe your wife went to somebody's house and you don't like that family, and you say, "Wallahi, if you go again, I will divorce you." SubhanAllah, what type of marriage is this? But suppose you said it; what do you do now?

Now, you mentioned Allah's name. You're not going to get away scot-free, you're not going to get away scot-free, because you brought in the name of Allah. If you simply said, "If you go there, I will divorce you," there's no name of Allah. You made a mistake, you say astaghfirullah, move on, end of story. But you mentioned the name of Allah. You brought it in; nobody told you to bring it in. Now you have to give kaffarah. Is that clear? This is scenario one. What the kaffarah is, we will come to.

Scenario two: it's not that you saw a better option; it's simply that you, as a human being, are not able to do what you promised to do. You made this sincere intention. Let me give a simple example: suppose you both, in a state of being good brothers, said, "We will visit each other every week." Life happens. You move apart, you move to a different location, whatever. You get my point, okay? You shouldn't have done that, you know; you brought in Allah subhanahu wa ta'ala. Now you are 'ajiz to do it.

In this case, to the level of your incapacity, you must repent. If it is truly beyond your control, there is no repentance. But if you are falling short, for example, because you don't like the guy, that's different than falling short because he moved away, right? If you're falling short because of tensions between you and him... I'm giving an example that we understand: "Wallahi, we're going to visit weekly." Suppose, as I said, there was tension between the two. You made up, you said, "Okay, from now on, we swear by Allah we will be in touch every week, every month." Then another tension happens, and both of you... it looks like this, like he's saying, "We have gone apart."

Obviously, before I answer: try your best for sulh. Always be the better of the two. Don't cut off ties. Nonetheless, it happens. My point is: if it happens because of you, you are guilty to the extent that you are not fulfilling the oath, in which case **you must also do tawbah along with the kaffarah.**

This is my point. Scenario one: there is no tawbah. You're choosing the better option; there is no tawbah, you just do the kaffarah. Scenario two: it's not the better option, but you are 'ajiz; you cannot do it, for whatever reason. In this case you must repent to Allah. And repentance: you feel guilty, you do istighfar, you make an intention, you learn your lesson, you're not going to do it again. This is tawbah. And on top of that, you do kaffarah. So both scenarios have kaffarah.

What is the kaffarah? Allah says in the Qur'an, Surah al-Ma'idah verse 89 (memorize it): Allah is going to forgive the laghw, but Allah will call you to task for the mun'aqidah, for the serious one. Fa-kaffaratuhu (this is in the Qur'an): if you're not able to fulfill the oath, fa-kaffaratuhu, number one, feed ten people the average meal of what you feed your family. Number two, clothe ten people, the average of what you clothe your family. Number three, freeing a slave; there is no number three in our time, so that's gone. If you don't have the financial means to pay for ten people's food or for ten people's clothing, you must fast three days. This is the kaffarah of your oath, if you are not able to do it. But Allah reminds us: try your best to fulfill your oaths. Don't use it in vain.

So, response: dear brother, you have two options, and inshallah all of us can afford them. If you really cannot financially afford it, then you move to number four, which is fasting three days. Number three, there is none: freeing a slave. The two options, and you may do either one; both of them are equally valid.

Feeding ten people what you normally eat. What do you normally eat? Some rice and some meat is our normal food, let's say. Okay? Or, mashallah, hamburger and french fries: a normal meal. The point is, what is the average meal, min awsat. Look at Allah's mercy. He could have said the most expensive, when you go to the five-star cuisine. Or if He didn't say anything, some lazy people would have said, "Okay, sometimes when I'm really hungry I eat a granola bar, so I'll give ten granola bars." No. Allah says: the average meals that you feed your own family. So ten meals must be fed to poor people.

And if you want to, you can go to option two. Option two is what? Ten clothings to poor people. So the average clothing item, you know, in Arab lands, in Pakistan, in America: the average that your family will wear, you will buy and you will give to people. This is the kaffarah of your yamin.
